> Is this new feature required because `IRouteValuesFeature` and `IEndpointFeature` are no longer available after an exception?

issue_context.title: Allow save errored request information before ExceptionHandlerMiddleware clears HttpContext
issue_context.body:
<!--

More information on our issue management policies can be found here: https://aka.ms/aspnet/issue-policies

-->

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
I'm trying to write a custom exception handler middleware based on the out of the box one but allows converting exceptions to responses by convention. 

One thing I'm struggling with is the `ExceptionHandlerMiddleware` currently [clears endpoint and route information](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/master/src/Middleware/Diagnostics/src/ExceptionHandler/ExceptionHandlerMiddleware.cs#L109) before it runs the `ExceptionHandler` delegate, so it is impossible to save information about the errored request in the `ExceptionHandler`.

For example, if I have a controller action decorated with my own exception handling metadata:
```
class MyController : Controller
{
    [MapException("error-handler-path")]
    public IActionResult MyAction() { }
}
```
The `MapException` attribute is cleared before my `ExceptionHandler` runs, so I have no chance to access the attribute.

The current workaround I'm using is adding a middleware after the `ExceptionHandlerMiddleware`, which extracts information I need before propagating the exception. You could see it [here](https://github.com/weichch/ExceptionMapper/blob/master/src/libraries/RabbitSharp.ExceptionMapper.AspNetCore/EndpointExceptionMappingMiddleware.cs#L67).

But, I don't like it. The extra middleware looks identical to `ExceptionHandlerMiddleware`, and it seems to me the same exception capturing process now happens in two different middleware components, and obviously mine is redundant if the default `ExceptionHandlerMiddleware` allows me to save request information before it clears HTTP context.

### Describe the solution you'd like
A new option in `ExceptionHandlerOptions` which allows access to the errored `HttpContext` before it gets cleared out.

For example:
```
public class ExceptionHandlerOptions
{
    public Action<HttpContext>? BeforeClearHttpContext { get; set; }
}
```

We could discuss the solution if the feature is not narrowly defined, and I'm happy to assist with the implementation if possible.

Hmm, the route values collection is currently cleared rather than replaced. That makes capturing it problematic. It might be better to null out the property and let routing make a new one. 
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/ca1f9f532f540f16732e8d8b4990fbae1578786b/src/Middleware/Diagnostics/src/ExceptionHandler/ExceptionHandlerMiddleware.cs#L156

> It might be better to null out the property

That would be a breaking change?

In my code, I create a copy of the route values using `RouteValueDictionary.FromArray(routeValues.ToArray())` before it gets cleared out.

> > It might be better to null out the property
> 
> That would be a breaking change?

I don't know if that feature is expected to be populated or not. We could also remove the IRouteValuesFeature which would avoid the issue since the app needs to be prepared for the feature not to be there.

That sounds feasible. If IEndpointFeature and IRouteValuesFeature are not set then there's no need to set IExceptionHandlerEndpointFeature either.

Go ahead and try it.

review_comments: If there are route values for the request then take a copy.
I think this should continue to clear. Otherwise, I'm pretty sure a new RouteValuesDictionary will be allocated per request.
What's the difference between making our own copy and clearing vs capturing the original and nulling it out? Don't you end up with the same number of allocations?

Ohh, this is happening in the exception filter and only if there is an exception.

In that case it doesn't matter.
